environmentNotes: First attempt: another agent's project held 127.0.0.1:23330, 23331 and 23335, and the host address pools were exhausted, so the first starting-build start failed on a port bind before any fixture existed. That project (openlaw-docs-d029r21-lc-upgrade) was removed with its own down -v and its log discarded. The run moved to 23338 (upgrade), 23339 (recovery) and Mailpit UI 23333.

A first fixture used record names without the DOC-029r2 prefix. It was removed with the project's own down -v before any upgrade step, and the fixture was rebuilt with 'DOC-029r2 operator-lifecycle' names. Its populate steps below are kept for the record.

Compose created the upgrade project's networks itself. For the recovery project the host had no free address pool, so the script pre-created its two networks with subnets 10.239.72.0/24 and 10.239.73.0/24 and the Compose project and network labels (see networkFallback). Compose file, services and network names stayed as the articles define them.
An owned Mailpit (openlaw-docs-d029r21-lc-mail, alias lc-mail) on the default bridge was joined to each project's backend network and was the controlled relay recipient.
Production authentication rate limits stayed on. No sign-in needed a retry in this run.
The candidate build step took 2 s: every layer came from the host build cache. Compose 5.5.1 applied this project's label, so the image IDs below are this project's.

Installation directories were fresh clones of https://github.com/juggernog20/OpenLaw.git under /tmp/claude-1000/openlaw-docs-lc-r2-1. Keys, fixture passwords, backups and clones stayed there and were deleted after teardown. No browser storage state was saved.
observations: Upgrade start: readiness after 4 s. The first migration line was 'migrations: reconciled 0090_onboarding_reviewed_types; continuing with pending migrations'; the journal then held 139 rows. The worker restarted once (RestartCount 1) after a failed auto_doc_generations query at startup, then logged 'OpenLaw worker started' and ran. Same as round 1.

The Contributor became a Business User through migration 0109. Staff API reach changed from 200/404/404 to 403/403/403; portal reach was 200/404/404, the same reach as before. It signed in with its password and landed on /portal/onboarding.

The relay was saved on the starting build as a legacy smtpUrl and smtpFrom. After the upgrade to 57e77e38 (discrete SMTP fields in Settings) the test email through that saved relay still returned 200 and reached the controlled recipient.

The recovery target on the starting build showed 'Something went wrong. The page could not load. Reload to try again.' at /login in headless Chromium, as in round 1. Its checks used the HTTP sign-in API through the same origin.
